subject: Q4 Renewal: Cross‑quarter Cohort Alignment & Prorate Check
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@stellarnet.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@stellarnet.com, Kyle Watson <kyle.watson@stellarnet.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q4 Renewal: Cross‑quarter Cohort Alignment & Prorate Check

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the renewal summary you sent last week. We're working through fiscal mapping across two cohorts and want to avoid a large mid‑Q spike. Two asks from our side:

1) Can you provide a prorate example if we co‑term Cohort A and B to our FY starting 01‑Oct (we'd prefer minimal disruption this quarter).
2) What does a staged ramp look like if we spread the uplift over the next 6 months vs. over 18 months?

Attached is our current usage snapshot. Procurement is looped for billing timing constraints. Would it be possible to get a short table with invoice timing / prorated amounts by cohort?

Best,
Elena
Director, Cloud Ops
Stellarnet Inc.

[attachment: "stellarnet_usage_snapshot.pdf (pdf)"]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@stellarnet.com>
Cc: Kyle Watson <kyle.watson@stellarnet.com>, procurement@stellarnet.com
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q4 Renewal: Cross‑quarter Cohort Alignment & Prorate Check

Elena — thanks, this is straightforward to model. I've attached a quick prorate table with three scenarios and the associated invoice phasing:

• Option A — Immediate co‑term to 01‑Oct with single prorated invoice to align Cohort A & B (one‑time prorate).
• Option B — Staged ramp (6 months): ramp additional capacity in equal monthly increments; small monthly credit applied to first two invoices.
• Option C — Staged ramp (18 months): slower growth with lower immediate cash impact, slightly higher unit price in yr1.

High level recommendation: if procurement needs a smoother cash profile, Option B gives a balance of predictable increase and limited upfront credit exposure. If finance wants to avoid an FY hit entirely, Option A minimizes timing complexity but creates a larger single invoice in early Oct.

Next steps: I can run exact dollar prorates once you confirm whether you want us to: (1) invoice the prorate in the Oct billing cycle, or (2) apply a credit to the Sep invoice and start fresh in Oct.

Attached: renewal_prorate_table.xlsx (worked example).

Available for a 30‑minute call tomorrow between 9–11 PT to walk procurement through the numbers.

— Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

[attachment: "renewal_prorate_table.xlsx (spreadsheet)"]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Stellarnet renewal: internal recommendation + quick asks

Team — looping you in with the customer's ask and the prorate examples I shared. Quick summary and asks so we have a unified position for tomorrow's call:

Background: Stellarnet wants to align two cohorts to their FY (01‑Oct). They are open to either a one‑time co‑term prorate or a staged ramp that spreads the uplift. Procurement's primary constraint is invoice timing (cannot absorb a large single charge in Oct).

My read: recommend Option B (6‑month staged ramp) with a small upfront credit to soften month 1. Operationally we should:
• Offer a 6% volume discount band for the staged ramp (applies once they hit the second month of the ramp).
• Include an auto‑renew opt-in on the amendment so billing cadence doesn't require another manual co‑term next year.
• Canary the increased capacity on a single model route for month 1 to monitor latency/cost impact.

Asks:
• Marissa — can you confirm if 6% sits within our allowable discount band for this ACV? If not, what's the max we can offer without deal desk?
• Grace — CS to own the canary monitoring and the rollout checklist; can you prepare a short ops runbook for the first 30 days?
• Rishi — please pre‑review the proposed_amendment_redline.pdf and flag any SSO/KMS language we should surface to procurement.

I'll include the redline in the follow up to the customer after we agree the discount/credit pattern.

Thanks — Jonas

[attachment: "proposed_amendment_redline.pdf (pdf)"]

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@stellarnet.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@stellarnet.com, Kyle Watson <kyle.watson@stellarnet.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 17:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 Renewal: Cross‑quarter Cohort Alignment & Prorate Check

Jonas — thanks for the clear options and for looping your team. Procurement reviewed Option A and B; finance prefers a staged approach to avoid a big hit in Oct. We are comfortable moving forward with Option B (6‑month staged ramp) with the following clarifications:

1) Apply the small upfront credit to the Oct invoice (we prefer credit vs delayed invoice).
2) Include the proposed 6% staged discount once month 2 of the ramp starts.
3) We want the auto‑renew clause in the amendment but with an explicit 30‑day notice to opt out prior to renewal.

Let's lock these items on a short call tomorrow at 10:00 PT. Once confirmed, procurement will sign the amendment and we can schedule the canary run with CS.

Best,
Elena
Director, Cloud Ops | Stellarnet Inc.
